```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.5,
                      message = FALSE)
```

This vignette walks through a typical analysis with OverReact: cleaning inputs,
describing the study population, estimating prevalence, fitting crude and adjusted
models, plotting them and exporting the results. It uses simulated data.

```{r setup}
library(OverReact)
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(123)
```

## Simulated data

```{r data}
n <- 1000
dat <- data.frame(
  age_years = round(rnorm(n, mean = 50, sd = 15)),
  sex = factor(sample(c("Female", "Male"), n, replace = TRUE)),
  region = factor(sample(c("North", "Midlands", "South"), n, replace = TRUE,
                         prob = c(0.30, 0.30, 0.40))),
  deprivation = factor(sample(paste0("Q", 1:5), n, replace = TRUE), levels = paste0("Q", 1:5)),
  smoking_status = factor(sample(c("Never", "Former", "Current"), n, replace = TRUE,
                                 prob = c(0.55, 0.25, 0.20)),
                          levels = c("Never", "Former", "Current")),
  exposure_primary = rnorm(n),
  bmi = rnorm(n, mean = 27, sd = 4),
  follow_up_years = runif(n, 0.5, 3),
  sample_date_chr = format(as.Date("2022-01-01") + sample(0:120, n, replace = TRUE), "%d/%m/%Y"),
  binary_1_2 = sample(c(1, 2), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.25, 0.75)),
  continuous_dirty = ifelse(runif(n) < 0.03, -1, rnorm(n, mean = 10, sd = 3))
)

linpred <- -1.1 + 0.55 * dat$exposure_primary + 0.03 * (dat$age_years - 50) +
  0.35 * (dat$sex == "Male") + 0.45 * (dat$smoking_status == "Current") +
  0.25 * (dat$region == "North")
dat$outcome_bin <- rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = plogis(linpred))
dat$outcome_group <- factor(dat$outcome_bin, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Negative", "Positive"))
dat$infections <- rpois(n, dat$follow_up_years * exp(-1 + 0.3 * dat$exposure_primary))
dat$severity <- factor(sample(c("None", "Mild", "Severe"), n, replace = TRUE),
                       levels = c("None", "Mild", "Severe"))

dat$region[sample(seq_len(n), 15)] <- NA
dat$smoking_status[sample(seq_len(n), 20)] <- NA
attr(dat$exposure_primary, "label") <- "Primary exposure score"

labels <- c(age_years = "Age (years)", sex = "Sex", region = "Region",
            smoking_status = "Smoking status", bmi = "Body mass index",
            deprivation = "Deprivation quintile")
```

## Cleaning helpers

The cleaners recode survey-style values: `binaryCleaner()` maps 1/2 to 1/0,
`continuousCleaner()` drops values below a floor, and `dateCleaner()` treats
the REACT missing-value codes as missing.

```{r cleaning}
data.frame(
  raw_binary = dat$binary_1_2[1:6],
  binary = binaryCleaner(dat$binary_1_2[1:6]),
  raw_continuous = round(dat$continuous_dirty[1:6], 2),
  continuous = continuousCleaner(dat$continuous_dirty[1:6], floornumber = 0),
  date = dateCleaner(dat$sample_date_chr[1:6], dateFormat = "%d/%m/%Y")
)
```

## Describing the population

`tableOne()` summarises each variable overall and by group. With
`statistical_test = TRUE`, the tests follow the data (Fisher's exact test for
sparse tables, Kruskal-Wallis for medians), and `smd = TRUE` adds standardised
mean differences.

```{r table-one}
table_one <- tableOne(
  dat = dat,
  rowvars = c("age_years", "bmi", "sex", "smoking_status", "region"),
  colvar = "outcome_group",
  cov_names = labels,
  statistical_test = TRUE,
  smd = TRUE
)
knitr::kable(table_one, digits = 3)
attr(table_one, "tests")
```

`tableOneDisplay()` turns the result into a gt table for HTML, or a flextable for Word.

```{r table-one-display, eval = requireNamespace("gt", quietly = TRUE)}
tableOneDisplay(table_one, output = "gt", title = "Characteristics by outcome")
```

## Prevalence

`makeTablesNew()` estimates prevalence with Wilson intervals. Its defaults apply no
assay correction; supply `sens` and `spec` to correct for test performance.

```{r prevalence}
prevalence <- makeTablesNew(
  dat = dat,
  result_var = "outcome_bin",
  covariates = c("sex", "smoking_status"),
  cov_name_list = labels,
  output_list = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(prevalence)
```

## Crude and adjusted models

`ModelMakerMultiRD()` fits each predictor in turn, adding adjusters one at a time.
For a binary outcome it also gives marginal risk differences and, with
`include_rr = TRUE`, marginal risk ratios. Every table carries Benjamini-Hochberg
q-values within each adjustment stage.

```{r models}
models <- ModelMakerMultiRD(
  dat = dat,
  list_of_variables_of_interest = c("exposure_primary", "smoking_status", "bmi"),
  outcome = "outcome_bin",
  joint_adjustment_vars = c("age_years", "sex", "region"),
  cov_name_list = labels,
  include_rd = TRUE,
  include_rr = TRUE,
  ncores = 1
)
knitr::kable(models$df_output)
knitr::kable(head(models$plot_output[, c("Variable", "Category", "adjustment_label",
                                         "OR", "Lower", "Upper", "P_value", "Q_value")]),
             digits = 3)
```

The `family` argument selects other models: Poisson rates with an offset,
risk ratios from a modified Poisson model, and ordinal or multinomial models for
categorical outcomes.

```{r families}
rates <- ModelMakerMultiRD(dat, "exposure_primary", outcome = "infections",
                           joint_adjustment_vars = c("age_years", "sex"),
                           family = "poisson", offset = "follow_up_years", ncores = 1)
knitr::kable(rates$df_output)

severity <- ModelMakerMultiRD(dat, "smoking_status", outcome = "severity",
                              joint_adjustment_vars = "age_years", ncores = 1)
knitr::kable(severity$df_output)
```

## Forest plots

`plotReactForest()` takes batch results, plotting data or fitted models.
`show_estimates = TRUE` prints each row's estimate, interval, p-value and N.

```{r forest}
plotReactForest(
  models,
  adjustment_numbers = c(0, 3),
  adjustment_descriptions = c("Crude", "Adjusted for age, sex and region"),
  show_estimates = TRUE,
  title = "Associations with the outcome"
)
```

```{r forest-rd}
plotReactForest(models, effect = "RD", adjustment_numbers = c(0, 3),
                adjustment_descriptions = c("Crude", "Adjusted"),
                title = "Marginal risk differences")
```

Fitted models can be compared directly; each list element becomes one adjustment level.

```{r forest-models}
model_list <- list(
  Crude = glm(outcome_bin ~ exposure_primary + smoking_status, binomial, dat),
  Adjusted = glm(outcome_bin ~ exposure_primary + smoking_status + age_years + sex,
                 binomial, dat)
)
plotReactForest(model_list, variables = c("exposure_primary", "smoking_status"))
```

## Automated report

`run_auto_tableone_regressions()` combines the descriptive table and the models, and
writes a short report ranking each predictor's most-adjusted association.

```{r report, results = "asis"}
auto <- run_auto_tableone_regressions(
  dat = dat,
  outcome = "outcome_bin",
  covariates = c("age_years", "sex"),
  independent_variables = c("exposure_primary", "smoking_status", "bmi", "age_years"),
  include_rd = TRUE,
  ncores = 1
)
cat(auto$report_markdown)
```

## Themes and palettes

```{r themes}
ggplot(dat, aes(x = sex, y = exposure_primary, fill = sex)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_imperial(palette = "cool") +
  theme_react() +
  labs(title = "theme_react() with an Imperial palette", x = NULL, y = "Primary exposure score")
```

## Export

Exports write to the paths you give; here, a temporary directory.

```{r export}
out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "overreact-vignette")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveREACTtable(prevalence, outpath = out_dir, filename = "prevalence")
savePrettyExcelWorkbook(list(`Table 1` = table_one, Prevalence = prevalence),
                        workbookName = "tables", outpath = out_dir)
sort(list.files(out_dir))
```
